analytical_observations: 1d direct SAMPLES: 273 monthly selected marks and 70000 scanned rows versus 20 daily marks and 5000 scanned rows (13.65x marks, 14x rows), EXPLAIN shows MinMax on day parts 1/14; 1d direct CPU 10.006 vs3.118ms.
1d broad full PromQL: 291 monthly selected marks versus 38 daily, 210000 versus145000 scanned rows; p50 67.9815ms vs55.4465ms (1.2261x), CPU 118.02025 vs83.44425ms (1.4144x).
14d full window: monthly SAMPLES 273 marks vs daily 280, native broad p50 essentially unchanged; 14d stage p50 57.4865 vs59.423ms (slower daily), no global promotion.

Metadata TAGS/TimeRanges retained: 70000+70000 read rows for broad queries; physical SAMPLES savings do not remove those scans. This is a new R05 time-gating hypothesis, not proof of R05 optimization.

On this single merged synthetic fixture day SAMPLES compressed storage bytes 1422855 vs month 2289798 (37.86% smaller), but 14 vs1 parts and unpaired single-pass ingest/merge; do not extrapolate to production storage or write costs.
limitations: Only 70000 synthetic one-sample/ID series, one month, source O1 not production O2, one machine, no replication, no 1/4/8 client throughput or p99
No fresh-server A/B/B/A for allocator/RSS, no steady-state write/merge CPU, partition fanout may regress under ongoing ingestion
Result only supports short-window schema-specific gains; cannot claim 14x end-to-end speed
raw_full_report_location: GitHub Actions uploaded artifact evidence/r15/report.json; includes every 144 query trial, create DDL, ingest and OPTIMIZE wall times, exact physical parts, EXPLAIN text
